claim: Single-chambered foraminiferal tests (Lagena etc.) take the surface-tension forms of Ch. V (flask/unduloid-like surfaces of revolution), chamber form preceding spiral coiling.

pre_scouted.name: Kireenko et al. (2022) BDJ Fig. 19 (Wikimedia Commons)

used.name: Thompson (1917) Fig. 84 Lagena after Brady — IA leaf 0276 (p. 256)
Kireenko et al. (2022) BDJ Fig. 19 — Lagena/Oolina/Fissurina monothalamic tests

verdict_rule: supported >= 75 % / refuted <= 25 % of unilocular tests Delaunay-compatible; mixed otherwise; untestable if every polythalamous control passes
specificity_caveat: 1/2 polythalamous controls pass the same gate: a smooth egg-shaped outline is close to a sphere+unduloid composite whether or not the shell is a single surface-tension chamber, so a passing flask-like test is 'consistent with' the catalogue, not a unique demonstration; the spindle refutation (bead aspect bound) is the specific result.
interpretation: Flask-shaped and globular unilocular tests (Lagena, Oolina, Fissurina) are reproduced by Thompson's own 'unduloid combined with a portion of a sphere' composite to within the free-form noise floor; the slender fusiform Lagena (L/W > pi) cannot be any single unduloid (bead aspect bound, Lean-checked) and are not fitted by any catalogue composite. Thompson's claim therefore holds for the flask morphotype he describes and fails for the spindle morphotype he also figures.
